artists.biography:
Steven John Wilson (born 3 November 1967) is an English musician, best known as the founder, lead guitarist, singer and songwriter of progressive rock band Porcupine Tree. He is involved in many other bands and musical projects both as musician and producer (including No-Man and Blackfield) and also maintains a solo career.
Wilson is a self-taught producer, audio engineer, guitar and keyboard player, playing other instruments as and where required (including bass guitar, concert harp, hammered dulcimer and flute).
He used to split his living time between Tel Aviv and London, England, but he no longer holds a permanent residence in Tel Aviv.

perplexity.description:
The Future Bites, released in 2021, is the sixth studio album by British musician Steven Wilson, issued through Caroline International and Arts & Crafts. Originally scheduled for June 2020, its release was delayed due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Musically, the album marks a stylistic shift for Wilson, embracing a blend of rock with strong electronic influences, including dance and neo-disco elements, while maintaining a rock edge. This evolution reflects Wilson’s exploration of themes such as identity and technology, presenting a nuanced commentary on contemporary life that balances critique with moments of optimism.

In the context of Wilson’s discography, The Future Bites stands out as a conceptually ambitious work that diverges from his earlier progressive rock and more guitar-driven albums. Co-produced with David Kosten, it incorporates modern production techniques and a sleek, futuristic sound palette. Critically, the album was noted for its innovative approach and thematic depth, receiving positive attention for its boldness and relevance. Commercially, it performed well in several European markets, reaching high chart positions such as number 2 in Austria and the Netherlands, and placing within the top 20 in Belgium and Australia.
